blocks.intro: Basement water usually comes from one of these:

tiles.body: Worn out, stuck or without power.
Water rising through the floor drain.
A basement bath basin that filled up.

tiles.h3: A Burst Pipe or Water Heater

blocks.intro: In June 2021, a storm flooded streets that normally stay dry, and a homeowner near County Line Road and Walnut Street had about 3 feet of water in a basement that had never flooded before.

items.h3: Never Flooded Doesn't Mean Never Will
items.body: Heavy, fast storms can overwhelm systems that have worked for decades.
Water damage downstairs often means flooring, drywall and furniture.
Groundwater and sewer water need different fixes.

bodies: Some basement water is a plumbing problem and some is a foundation problem. We handle the plumbing side: [sump pumps](/hinsdale/sump-pumps), battery backups, discharge lines, backflow valves and [overhead sewer systems](/hinsdale/overhead-sewer-systems).
If water is coming through cracks in the walls, a waterproofing contractor is the right call, and we'll tell you so. Fixing the plumbing first often solves more than you'd expect.

blocks.h2: When a Basement Floods for the First Time
blocks.body: In June 2021, a storm sent water bubbling out of a sewer in northeast Hinsdale, and one home had about 3 feet of water in a basement that had never flooded before. That's a reminder that a dry past doesn't promise a dry future. If your basement is finished, protection like a backflow valve, an overhead sewer or a sump pump with a backup is worth considering before the next big storm.

blocks.h2: Basement Flooding Questions From Hinsdale Homeowners

items.q: Is it groundwater or sewer water?
items.preview: Where it comes in tells you.
items.answer: Water at the walls or rising in the sump pit is groundwater. Water coming up through the floor drain is usually sewer water.

items.q: Our basement had never flooded. Why now?
items.preview: Storms are heavier, and equipment ages.
items.answer: A storm heavier than usual, a pump at the end of its life or a partly blocked line can all change things. We'll find out which.

items.q: Do you dry out flooded basements?
items.preview: We fix the cause. Restoration companies dry and clean.
items.answer: We fix the pump, pipe or drain. For water removal and drying, a restoration company is the right call.

items.q: What's the best protection for a finished basement?
items.preview: A good pump, a backup and a backflow valve.
items.answer: A reliable sump pump with a battery backup, plus a backflow valve. For repeat sewer backups, an overhead sewer.

items.q: How much does basement flooding repair cost in Hinsdale?
items.preview: It depends on the cause. You'll approve a flat price first.
items.answer: It depends on the cause and what needs to be repaired or added. You'll approve a flat-rate price before we start.
